name: NOTABLe
question: Does percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation reduce fecal incontinence severity more than sham stimulation in women after first-line treatment?

design.population: 166 women with moderate-to-severe fecal incontinence despite supervised pelvic muscle training and constipating medication were randomized at nine US Pelvic Floor Disorders Network sites.
design.locator: Zyczynski 2022, Methods: Study Design and Oversight, Participants; Results: Study Population

verdictNote: The primary St. Mark's severity-score comparison did not meet superiority.
takeaway: In women with fecal incontinence after first-line treatment, 12 weekly sessions of percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation did not improve St. Mark's severity scores significantly more than sham stimulation (adjusted difference −1.3 points, 95% CI −2.8 to 0.2).

reports.label: Primary 12-week report
reports.citation: Zyczynski HM, Richter HE, Sung VW, et al. "Percutaneous Tibial Nerve Stimulation vs Sham Stimulation for Fecal Incontinence in Women: NeurOmodulaTion for Accidental Bowel Leakage Randomized Clinical Trial." *Am J Gastroenterol.* 2022;117(4):654-667. doi:10.14309/ajg.0000000000001605

results.endpoint: St. Mark's fecal incontinence severity score
results.measure: Adjusted mean change from baseline after 12 sessions; adjusted mean difference in change, PTNS minus sham, points
results.note: The seven-item score ranges from 0–24; higher scores indicate worse symptoms. The within-group minimal important difference is 3–5 points. The model used a two-sided 0.05 superiority threshold.
results.locator: Results: Primary Outcome; Table 2; Methods: Outcome Measures, Statistical Analysis

results.measure: Adjusted mean change from baseline after 12 sessions; adjusted mean difference in change, PTNS minus sham, episodes per week
results.note: Diary-based secondary outcome; no multiplicity adjustment for secondary outcomes.
results.locator: Results: Secondary Outcomes; Table 2; Methods: Statistical Analysis

results.endpoint: At least 50% fewer weekly fecal incontinence episodes
results.measure: Diary-complete responders after 12 sessions; unadjusted odds ratio
results.note: Secondary endpoint among participants with complete bowel diaries.

harms.label: Serious adverse events
harms.note: None of the six serious adverse events was treatment related.

harms.label: Paresthesia
harms.note: Percentages are rounded as reported by the authors.

harms.label: Needle-site bleeding and pain
harms.note: Both events were reported only in the active PTNS arm.

delivery.label: Eligibility
delivery.value: Symptoms for at least three months and St. Mark's score at least 12 after run-in; exclusions included predominant uncontrolled diarrhea or severe constipation, unrepaired rectovaginal fistula or fourth-degree obstetric laceration, rectal prolapse, and prior colon resection.

delivery.label: Run-in and randomization
delivery.value: Four-week education and bowel-diary run-in; 199 entered, 170 were eligible, and 166 were randomized 2:1 at nine US sites.
delivery.locator: Methods: Study Design and Oversight, Intervention; Results: Study Population

delivery.label: Active and sham procedure
delivery.value: Twelve weekly 30-minute sessions on one lower extremity: needle-electrode PTNS with current titrated to toe twitch or sensation versus a retractable placebo needle plus fifth-metatarsal surface electrodes connected to TENS.

delivery.label: Treatment adherence
delivery.note: Adherence meant completing at least 10 of 12 sessions within 14 weeks.

delivery.label: Maintenance phase
delivery.value: A nine-month responder maintenance phase was planned; the protocol specified discontinuation if Part 1 failed to show superiority.

reports.label: Differential-response analysis
reports.citation: Luchristt D, Carper B, Balgobin S, et al. "Characteristics associated with subjective and objective measures of treatment success in women undergoing percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation vs sham for accidental bowel leakage." *Int Urogynecol J.* 2023;34(8):1715-1723. doi:10.1007/s00192-022-05431-y
reports.followUp: Outcomes after the randomized 12-week treatment course

results.endpoint: Differential PTNS response by baseline characteristics
results.measure: Treatment-by-characteristic interactions across St. Mark's score, patient impression, and diary response definitions
results.note: Isolated interactions varied across success definitions; models lacked multiplicity adjustment and subgroup power.

results.measure: Participants meeting all three success criteria among those with complete outcome data
results.note: Pooled PTNS and sham: 41/142 (29%). Criteria were St. Mark's response, patient global impression, and at least 50% fewer weekly episodes.

delivery.label: Analyzed participants
delivery.value: 160/166 randomized women had data for at least one success definition; 142/166 had complete data for all definitions.

relations.note: Both sham-controlled PTNS trials missed their prespecified primary fecal-incontinence efficacy endpoints.
